mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 3% YoY signals inflationary pressures that typically lead the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, which in turn increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL YoY growth exceeds 3% and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a single month indicates a weakening labor market, which is a leading indicator of economic slowdown and thus negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE increases by more than 0.5% MoM and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in housing starts (HOUST) for three consecutive months signals a weakening demand in the housing market, which is a strong indicator of a broader economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST declines for three consecutive months and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% MoM signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which typically leads to increased corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO increases by more than 1% MoM and S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals an easing monetary policy, which typically leads to increased liquidity in the market and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS decreases and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) both show a negative trend over three consecutive months, it indicates a weakening labor market and broader economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE and PAYEMS both decline for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: If both UNRATE and PAYEMS decline for three consecutive months and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in retail sales (RSAFS) coupled with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals strong consumer demand and a healthy labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases > 1% MoM and UNRATE decreases
failure_condition: If RSAFS increases by more than 1% MoM and UNRATE decreases, but S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, when the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 5%, it indicates a restrictive monetary policy that typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS exceeds 5% and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of the triggered instances.
